title: Just Enough Administration
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose of Just Enough Administration and define its core vocabulary.
Apply just enough administration in a small PowerShell example and predict its result.
Identify one relevant edge case, version constraint, or troubleshooting step.

content.intro: This lesson covers Just Enough Administration in the PowerShell learning path. It expands the supplied syllabus heading into an actionable draft with a visual, a worked example, and a short knowledge check.
content.why_it_matters: Secure automation begins by validating untrusted values and limiting the authority of the process. Do not put real secrets in source code or output; use approved identity and secret-store patterns, prefer least privilege, make administrative changes previewable, and record audit-relevant results.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety note
content_blocks.text: The main path targets modern PowerShell 7.6 LTS. Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatibility is labeled separately. Some providers, admin cmdlets and APIs depend on OS, module version, permissions or tenant access; the examples are static references, not proof of execution.
